title: BA1/1630/2023 of VIJAY YADAV ALIAS MANISH YADAV Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 1630 of 2023
Vijay Yadav alias Manish Yadav ........Applicant
Versus
State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent

Present:-
Mr. Rajveer Singh, Advocate for the applicant appeared
through video conferencing.
Mr. Vipul Painuli, Brief Holder for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Applicant Vijay Yadav alias Manish Yadav is in
judicial custody in FIR No.640 of 2022, dated 14.09.2022,
under Sections 323, 354(C), 376(2)(n), 506 IPC, Police
Station Kotwali Roorkee, District Haridwar. He has
sought his release on bail.
2. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
3. According to the FIR, the victim came into the
contact with the applicant through social media platform.
In the month of December, 2021 the applicant visited the
victim and thereafter, he established relations with her.
He also took her obscene and intimate photographs and
videos. Thereafter, he started blackmailing the victim and
continued physical relations with her. The FIR is quite in
detail and according to it, thereafter, the applicant on
multiple occasions under threat of making the intimate

2
videos viral established physical relations with her and, in
fact, the applicant did so. He sent nude messages to the
relatives of the victim and had posted the videos and
photographs on the social media platform.
4. Learned counsel for the applicant would
submit that the victim and applicant are major; the
applicant has not committed any rape; establishing
physical relations under the pretext of marriage is not an
offence of rape; the applicant has not uploaded the
intimate photographs of the victim.
5. Learned State counsel would submit that the
victim has supported the prosecution case. The applicant
had uploaded the intimated photographs on social media
platform.
6. It is the stage of bail. Much of the discussion
at this stage is to be avoided. To the extent of
appreciating the controversy the matter may be
examined with the caveat that any observation made at
this stage shall have no bearing at any subsequent
stage of the case.
7. Establishing physical relations by two
consenting adults may perhaps not attract any offence,

3
but if the physical relations are established under
misconception of facts, it may not be a free consent.
Those are different situations. But, in the instant case,
the story of the victim goes beyond it. According to the
victim, the applicant made video of intimacy and has also
taken photograph and while threatening her to make
those intimate photographs viral, he established physical
relations on multiple occasions with her; beaten her up
and finally he uploaded those photographs on social
media platform. It is really a very serious offence.
8. Having considered the facts and circumstances
of the case and other attending factors, this Court is of
the view that it is not a case fit for bail and the bail
application of the applicant deserves to be rejected.
9. The bail application is rejected.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 19.12.2023
Sanjay
